findings.body:
The PathPrefix move also unwraps `middleware.RequireRole("admin")`. `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` are now registered as bare `http.HandlerFunc`s, so any caller who can reach those URLs can list users and edit roles. The parent `routes()` function does not re-apply that middleware.

Keep the existing wrapper on each handler (or `Use` it on the v2 subrouter if `RequireRole` is a mux middleware). Restore `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` above the subrouter as well:

```suggestion
	v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
	v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

summary:
The PathPrefix move is the right gorilla/mux shape, but the same hunk drops the admin role check. Restore that wrapper before merge.

`r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()` plus `v2.Handle("/admin/...")` lands at `/api/v2/admin/users` and `/api/v2/admin/roles`. What is not a cleanup is removing `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` and registering `listUsers` / `editRoles` as bare `http.HandlerFunc`s. Those two routes previously required the admin role; after this change any caller who can hit the new paths can list users and POST role edits. Nothing else in the repo re-applies that middleware on the parent router.

The unversioned `/admin/users` and `/admin/roles` paths are gone with no shim. That matches the versioning intent, but clients still on those URLs will 404 until they switch.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The base routes wrapped listUsers/editRoles with middleware.RequireRole("admin"); the head PathPrefix move registers both as bare HandlerFuncs on the v2 subrouter with no authz wrapper or Use() call, so admin endpoints are unauthenticated.
